newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea banks consider aid to cash-short companies.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea banks consider aid to cash-short companies.

text.p: South Korean commercial banks are considering jointly helping finance liquidity-stricken companies for the benefit of the national economy, an official at the Korea Federation of Banks said on Tuesday.
Presidents of 10 domestic banks, including the state-funded Korea Developent Bank, have set a meeting at 3:00 p.m. (0600 GMT) to discuss further details, he said.
Senior officials at the banks agreed in principle to launch a committee, through which they will decide to support a financially troubled company or let it go bankrupt, the official said.
The committee will try to prevent bankruptcy if the company's problems are not serious, he said.

Korean financial institutions recently have been reluctant to extend fresh loans to companies rumoured to be experiencing serious cash shortages, leading to an increase in debt defaults among smaller companies.

South Korea's financial industry was hit hard by this year's collapse of the flagship affiliates of two big conglomerates, the Hanbo Group, which is at the centre of a growing national corruption scandal, and the Sammi Group.
The Jinro Group, the nation's 19th largest, was rumoured last week to be facing serious liquidity problems. The group said on Monday it would sell "unprofitable" business lines to generate more cash.
The bank committee plans to ask non-banking financial institutions to join the group.
